references.text: Moses' sister offered to find a Hebrew nurse, which led Pharaoh's daughter to give the instruction to take the child and nurse him.
After Moses was nursed, he was brought back to Pharaoh's daughter, who adopted him as her son.
Sarah nursed Isaac, another example of a mother nursing her own child in a special situation connected to God's plan.
Abraham's servant gave gifts as payment, similarly to how Pharaoh's daughter promised to give wages for the nursing.
Laban asked Jacob to set his wages, a similar theme about payment for services performed.
A nurse for Mephibosheth is mentioned, showing the practice of having nurses for children in Israel.
Isaiah prophesies about kings and queens who will be foster fathers and nurses for God's people, an image of care and nourishment.
Stephen's speech refers to how Moses was taken up by Pharaoh's daughter, confirming this historical account.
The book of Hebrews mentions how Moses' parents hid him in faith, which led to the events described in this verse.
A strong thematic contrast between life-giving care (Exodus) and despair over death (2 Kings), highlighting God's protection against human downfall.
A theological parallel showing how God's plan for leaders (Moses and Samuel) involves maternal care and protection before weaning.
